name: PT Japfa Comfeed Indonesia Tbk

frontmatter.title: Japfa Comfeed: an integrated protein chain priced for a trough
frontmatter.summary: Japfa is Indonesia's integrated poultry chain — feed, breeding, farm, processing — and the market pays a trough multiple for mid-cycle earnings. The nine-month filing shows revenue up by more than a fifth with the gross margin held despite dearer corn and soybean meal, while the balance sheet carries the inventory build that funded it. BUY, target Rp2,619, a return of 70.9%.
thesis: The earnings being discounted are the nine months already filed, not a forecast: net sales of IDR54,525.0bn, gross profit of IDR11,249.5bn and operating profit of IDR5,179.2bn. The cost links are calibrated to reproduce that margin rather than to assume a recovery [S3].

The data pack's depreciation is a fraction of the charge the LK books, so its EBITDA and every multiple built on it are wrong. Restating from the fixed-asset note lifts FY2025 EBITDA to IDR7,323.9bn and lowers the multiple the shares trade on [S4, F1].

Integration defends the margin: feed is repriced on input cost inside the year, and the farm, processing and consumer segments capture the spread the feed segment gives away. That is why dearer corn and meal did not break the gross margin [S3, S4].

The balance sheet is both the risk and the discount: gross debt rose with the inventory and advance build, and net debt reaches IDR16,481.2bn at our first forecast year end, 2.0x times EBITDA [S3, F22, F25].

The base case starts at the filed nine-month operating margin of 9.5% and then fades towards the through-cycle level, 7.4% by FY2030E, rather than carrying the strongest year on record into perpetuity; the payout is held at the declared ratio, not the peak [S3, S4, S6].

What we are paid for is the spread between the DCF, which now values the equity above the Rp1,620 price, and the multiple cross-checks at 7.2x trailing earnings and 6.4x EBITDA. The blend is the target; the red team should attack the multiple, not the actuals [S0, S3].

catalysts.event: Interim dividend paid; the first distribution under the working-capital build and the test of whether the company can pay while it borrows. The shares go ex on 6 November 2026 [S6].
FY2026 audited accounts due: whether the fourth quarter holds the nine-month margin and whether the inventory and advance build unwinds into cash [S3].
Agriculture ministry supervision of integrators tightens; any rule on live-bird pricing or placement quotas reaches the commercial farm directly [S7].

blocks.text: **BUY, target Rp2,619 against a price of Rp1,620: total return 70.9%, price upside 61.7%, on a market capitalisation of IDR18,961.9bn at the last close [S0].** We state the shape of that return at the outset because it is not evenly sourced. The engine's discounted cash flow values the equity at Rp1,847, above the Rp1,620 price; the P/E and EV/EBITDA cross-checks value it at Rp2,475 and Rp2,639, up 34.0% and 42.9% on the primary method [S0]. The cash-flow method therefore supports the price on its own, and the target is the weighted blend: the part of the return above the cash-flow value rests on the earnings multiple, and that is precisely where the red team should press.

**What the company has actually delivered.** Nine months to 30 September 2026: net sales of IDR54,525.0bn, gross profit of IDR11,249.5bn, operating profit of IDR5,179.2bn and profit for the period of IDR3,549.4bn before minorities [S3]. The nine-month gross margin of 20.6% was achieved while the deck's corn and soybean meal ran above the prior year, which is the single most informative line in this report: the cost increase was absorbed, not passed through to a lower margin [S3, deck.agri.corn, deck.agri.soymeal].

**The restatement that changes the multiples.** The pack carries FY2025 depreciation of IDR1,140.3bn; the fixed-asset note charges IDR1,140.3bn through the income statement, and the segment note is higher again once the right-of-use charge is added [S4, F1]. We restate the fixed-asset charge for both years, so FY2025 EBITDA is IDR7,323.9bn and the shares trade on 3.9x EV/EBITDA and 4.7x trailing earnings on the FY2025 year-end balance sheet. That is a year-end multiple, not today's: on the 30 September 2026 net debt the same FY2025A EBITDA gives a higher multiple, and the 4.4x is our FY2026E EBITDA on FY2026E forecast net debt of IDR16,481.2bn, not on that balance sheet [S0, S3, F25]. Both sit below the higher multiples a pack-sourced model would show [S0, S4]. A reader who takes the pack at face value will overstate this company's multiple and understate its cash conversion.

**Why the price is where it is.** The shares sit at the fifty-two week low of 1,620.0, down from 2,930.0, and the reason is in the balance sheet rather than the P&L. Inventories reached IDR14,355.3bn at the end of September, gross debt comprises IDR12,410.4bn of short-term bank loans, IDR5,332.9bn of non-current long-term loans and IDR487.5bn of bonds, and cash is IDR4,611.9bn [S3, F22, F23, F24, F25]. The market reads a company borrowing to hold corn as one whose earnings are not cash; we read a harvest-timed inventory position plus a named capital programme, both of which we model unwinding, and the bear case that they do not is priced in section five.

**The variant view, stated as a disagreement.** The shares are capitalising our first forecast year's earnings of Rp374 at 4.3x and its EBITDA at 4.4x [S0]. We think the right anchor is the margin range the company has actually printed, with the nine-month figure inside it, rather than the single best year or the single trough quarter. If the margin is mid-cycle and the working capital unwinds, the multiple is wrong and the target understates the value. If the margin is peak and the cash stays in inventory, the multiple is right and the target is too high. Both readings are in the target, and the second is why we no longer call the first conservative: the target is a blend of a DCF that now clears the price and two cross-checks that carry it further, and section four shows which is which.

Japfa Comfeed is an integrated poultry and animal-protein business. The LK reports six operating segments, and their external net sales for FY2025 were IDR24,513.8bn in the commercial farm, IDR15,786.7bn in animal feed, IDR10,647.8bn in poultry processing and consumer products, IDR5,137.2bn in aquaculture, IDR3,541.5bn in poultry breeding and IDR2,300.4bn in trading and others, before sales discounts [S4, F9, F10, F11, F12, F13, F14]. The chain runs from feed milling and grandparent stock through hatcheries and commercial farms into slaughter and further processing, and the consumer products arm sells branded chicken into modern and traditional trade [S2]. Exports are marginal at IDR1,339.6bn of FY2025 net sales; the rest is domestic [S4, F15].

The mix has moved toward the farm and processing end. Over the nine months to September 2026 the commercial farm booked IDR20,728.4bn, animal feed IDR15,662.8bn, processing and consumer products IDR9,831.5bn, aquaculture IDR4,381.3bn, breeding IDR3,106.3bn and trading IDR2,036.7bn [S3, F16, F17, F18, F19, F20, F21]. Feed and processing are the two fastest growing lines, which is the right direction for this model: feed transmits the corn and meal bill, processing holds the brand and the shelf. The commercial farm remains the largest single line, so group profit still depends on the live-bird price even as the branded end grows.

The physical footprint is national and deliberately close to the crop. The annual report lists feed mills at Medan, Padang, Lampung, Cikande-Serang, Tangerang, Purwakarta, Cirebon, Grobogan, Sragen, Buduran and Gedangan in Sidoarjo, Banjarmasin and Makassar; corn-drying facilities outside the mills in Lampung, Brebes, Sumbawa, Bima, Makassar, Gowa, Sidrap, Gorontalo and Kotamobagu; and slaughterhouses from Medan and Lampung through Cikupa, Parung, Sadang, Pemalang, Pabelan, Magelang, Yogyakarta and Boyolali [S2]. Aquafeed mills and shrimp hatcheries extend the same model to aquaculture, and the animal-vaccine and premix plants supply the group's own farms first [S2]. The corn dryers are the part that matters for the margin: they let the company buy at harvest and store, which is why inventories here are a strategic position rather than a pure working-capital item [S2, S3].

Capital allocation in the year under review was additive rather than maintenance. The company built a hatchery at Berau in East Kalimantan, a second slaughterhouse at Pemalang, rebuilt farms at Palembang and Makassar with solid-wall ventilation, and added grandparent-stock capacity at Tanjung Bintang in Lampung [S2]. Those projects are why capital expenditure runs above the historical ratio in our first forecast year and why we do not model it falling straight back to the old rate [S2, S3].

The Indonesian poultry chain is best described as a set of integrators surrounded by independent
smallholders. Integrators own the feed mill, the breeding line and often the slaughterhouse; the
independent farmer buys chicks and feed and sells live birds into a market where the farm-gate price
is set daily and is notoriously volatile. Because feed is the largest cost in a broiler and corn is
the largest input in feed, the integrator earns a spread between the corn it buys and the chicken it
sells, and the two move for different reasons on different calendars. That is the structural reason
a feed-and-farm business reports swings between a thin margin and a fat one, and why a mid-cycle
margin rather than a best year is the right anchor for valuing it.

Ownership is concentrated in the Japfa group. The pack records insiders at 67.5% and a free float of 40.6%, figures that cannot both be right and which we flag rather than reconcile [S0]. The related-party evidence in the filing is direct: in September 2026 the company and its subsidiary PT Ciomas Adisatwa sold the whole of the animal-vaccine business, PT Vaksindo Satwa Nusantara, to Japfa Pte. Ltd. and Bionovus Pte. Ltd., entities under common control, for gross proceeds of IDR1,807.4bn [S3, F29]. A related-party disposal of a technology subsidiary is the most important governance fact in this report, because it shows both that the group transacts with the listed company and that the company is willing to sell to it.

Demand is a staples story with a cyclical price on top. Poultry is the cheapest widely available animal protein in Indonesia, consumption per head rises with income, and the addressable market therefore grows faster than the population; that is what supports the deck's long-run real growth assumption of 5.29% [S2, deck.macro.gdp_real_id]. Our terminal growth of 4.0% sits below it and below every explicit-year revenue growth in section three: the terminal rate is the model's own input, not the deck's real GDP growth, because a mature protein market tracks nominal incomes rather than the whole economy [S0, deck.macro.gdp_real_id]. But the price the producer receives is set in a live-bird market that clears daily, and this year has demonstrated how far it can move: in early November independent broiler farmers said farm-gate prices had fallen below their cost of production and warned of closures [S5]. That is the trough end of the same cycle that produced the group's strongest year.

The cost side is the deck. Corn for FY2026E sits at US$215/t against US$173/t for the last actual year, and soybean meal at US$411/t against US$321/t, stepping up again later in the explicit period to US$450/t [S0]. We do not override the deck; we charge four fifths of each input move into cost of goods sold, not the nine tenths a single nine-month comparison would allow. One period cannot separate pass-through from carried harvest inventory, and the four-year record argues against full pass-through: a high pass-through rate explains only a small part of the margin recovery of FY2023 to FY2024 even though corn fell by a quarter [S0, S3, S4]. The closest listed comparator, CPIN.JK, uses a lower rate on the same template; the gap reflects JPFA's larger processing and consumer share, which reprices on the shelf rather than the ration [S2, S4]. Our terminal growth of 4.0% is above CPIN's and below the deck's real GDP growth [deck.macro.gdp_real_id, m.cpi_id]. The rupiah is the second channel: soybean meal is imported and the deck carries the currency from Rp16,448/USD to Rp18,350/USD, so a weaker rupiah raises the meal bill even when the dollar price is flat [S0, S4].

Policy is an active variable rather than a background one. The agriculture ministry is tightening supervision of the integrators in the same period that farm-gate prices fell, and the state logistics agency is distributing subsidised corn to smallholder layer farmers [S7, S5]. Both point the same way: the state is intervening in the relationship between integrators and independent farmers, and its two instruments — placement rules and cheap corn — reach the commercial farm segment and the feed spread respectively. A floor price for live birds, a cap on placements or a corn channel that bypasses the integrator all land on this company.

Competition is concentrated but not static. The listed peer set for animal protein in Indonesia is small — this report's own section four cross-checks against the sector median — and the industry is dominated by a handful of integrated groups plus a long tail of independent mills [S0]. Within that group, Japfa's position rests on three things the annual report shows rather than claims: feed-mill coverage national enough to shorten the haul to the farm, corn drying at harvest that lowers the effective input cost, and a branded processed-chicken business that provides a second price point when the live-bird price is weak [S2].

The moat is a cost and distribution moat, not a brand moat. Feed is a commodity sold on formulation and price, so the defensible advantage is scale in milling, proximity to the corn crop and the working capital to buy at harvest — all three supported by the footprint [S2]. Processing and consumer products add a modest brand and shelf-space advantage, but that segment is a quarter of sales, not a majority, so it cannot carry the group alone [S4, F11]. On the five forces: buyer power is high in feed, where farmers switch on price, and lower in branded processed chicken; supplier power is high and concentrated in corn and soybean meal, which is why the deck matters this much; entry is moderate in milling and hard in integrated breeding and processing, where capital and biosecurity record are barriers; substitutes are other proteins, and poultry's price advantage protects it; and rivalry is intense, with the live-bird price the clearing mechanism [S2, S5].

Revenue is built from the filing, not from a growth assumption. Nine-month net sales of IDR54,525.0bn annualise to IDR73,696.8bn at our flat fourth-quarter assumption — growth of 21.4% — and then decelerate to 8.0% and below as this year's input-cost push is not repeated [S3, F5, deck.agri.corn].

The margin is the load-bearing assumption and it is the witnessed one. Gross profit of IDR11,249.5bn on the nine-month sales base is a gross margin of 20.6%, which is what the filing prints, and the two cost links are calibrated to deliver it rather than to assume it: we attribute US$215/t and US$411/t exposure through link shares with high pass-through, and the engine reproduces the witnessed margin [S3, F6]. Operating margin is 9.5% against 10.2% in the strongest year on record — a step down, and the one place our base case sits below the last actual, because the second half of FY2025 was the peak [S4, S3]. Selling, general and administrative expense is held near the nine-month ratio, and depreciation is the restated charge, a little under two per cent of revenue against the fraction of a per cent the pack implies [S4, F1].

Cash flow is where the story is uncomfortable and we do not smooth it. The nine-month cash-flow statement shows a working-capital outflow, and the balance sheet explains it: inventories of IDR14,355.3bn, up materially from the prior year end as the corn advance book and the price of corn rose [S3, F26]. We model operating working capital at roughly a quarter of revenue in the first forecast year and normalise it toward a fifth by the end of the explicit period, still above the FY2025 ratio because the biological assets and the drying operation have grown [S3, S4]. The consequence is free cash flow to the firm of IDR-5,746.9bn — negative — turning positive from the following year, and it is the reason the DCF is the lowest of our three methods rather than the middle one.

Debt is the other half of that sentence. The prior year end carried a large bond in current liabilities that has since been repaid, so the rise in the headline number is part refinancing and part new borrowing, and we carry the net increase as witnessed net borrowing in the first forecast year rather than pretending it did not happen [S3]. At IDR16,481.2bn of net debt and 2.0x times EBITDA the balance sheet is comfortable against the FY2023 trough, when the same ratio was far higher, but it is no longer the near-net-cash position the peak year produced [S0, S3]. Finance costs of IDR788.7bn for the nine months show what that costs in the P&L [S3, F28].

Capital allocation, in order of the cash: the working-capital build first, then capital expenditure of IDR5,623.1bn, or 7.6% of sales against 4.6% in FY2025, then the distribution [S0, S3]. The named projects are the hatchery, the slaughterhouse and the farm rebuilds in the annual report [S2]. The programme is why the ratio starts at the nine-month run-rate and falls to 3.0% of sales in the terminal year, which is depreciation plus growth on the asset base rather than a haircut [S3, S4]. We anchor the dividend on the declared policy rather than the peak-year payout: Rp150 a share against Rp140 declared for FY2025 [S0, S4, S6].

Earnings quality, run through the house screens. The accruals screen is clean over the three years to FY2025; the divergence appears only in the current year, and it is visible in the working-capital lines rather than hidden in a receivable [S0, S3]. The flags that fire are inventory outgrowing cost of sales — the corn position — and short-term debt funding working capital, both optics-class and both disclosed [S3, F22, F26]. One further item belongs here: the vaccine disposal was a common-control transaction for gross proceeds of IDR1,807.4bn, with the tax on the difference charged directly to equity and a far smaller residual — the net equity figure — recognised there. So the amount taken to equity is the residual, not the headline proceeds, and reported profit never saw any of it [S3, F29]. Because the disposal and the shareholder-loan repayment closed on 29 September 2026, both sit inside the 30 September balance sheet already, and about a fifth of net debt was retired inside the period we are valuing [S3, F29]. The IDX regime screen is clean — no special notation, monitoring board or suspension in the annual report's disclosure — and on the manipulation-versus-optics test there is no manipulation-class finding [S2].

The method set fits the business because this is an asset-heavy, working-capital-heavy integrator whose earnings swing with a commodity spread. A discounted cash flow prices the asset base and the cycle; a multiple cross-check prices what the market pays for those earnings at a point in the cycle. The industry configuration weights the DCF at 50% and the two multiples at 30% and 20% [S0]. Weighting cash flow at half is deliberate: the inventory build depresses free cash without changing earnings power, so a cash-flow-only view would be too harsh, while an earnings-only view would ignore that the cash has genuinely gone out.

The cost of capital is built rather than asserted. The risk-free rate is the deck's rupiah ten-year at 7.4%, the mature-market equity premium 4.2% and the Indonesia country risk premium 2.5%, applied to a levered beta of 1.6x derived from an industry unlevered beta of 0.9x at a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.0x on the current market capitalisation. That gives a cost of equity of 16.7% and, with the cost of debt at 9.4% pre-tax at a weight of 51%, a WACC of 12.0% [S0]. The cost of equity sits above the house band because the balance sheet is levered at about one times the market capitalisation; the WACC used to discount sits inside the band, and we have not adjusted it.

The primary method discounts free cash flow to the firm from the 30 September balance-sheet date, so the stub year carries only the final quarter of FY2026E, and it exits on a terminal growth rate of 4.0% with a terminal value share of 54.2% of enterprise value [S0]. That share is high, as it is for a capital-intensive business with long-lived assets, and it is the honest weakness of the method here. The implied exit multiple is the test the house card demands, and it fails: the terminal value on FY2035E EBITDA implies an exit multiple below the 6.4x the cross-check applies, so the gap between the DCF and the multiples is the exit multiple and the capex conversion as well as the discount rate. We no longer claim the divergence is a discount-rate effect. One further weakness is disclosed rather than left for a reader to find: holding the realised margin at the terminal level to FY2035E requires the constant-price input to be lifted by about a point above its FY2029E level, an improvement we do not source. If the terminal margin were instead allowed to fade to the level the cost-fit implies, the DCF would fall by roughly two-fifths; the target, which is half DCF, would fall by about an eighth and would remain above the Rp1,620 price. The held margin is the base, and the rating does not rest on it [S0, S3, S4, deck.agri.corn, deck.agri.soymeal].

The divergence is the finding and we state it rather than bury it: the DCF gives Rp1,847, the P/E cross-check Rp2,475, up 34.0%, and the EV/EBITDA cross-check Rp2,639, up 42.9% [S0]. The engine flags both. The cause is not a different view of the business: the P/E applies 7.2x earnings and the EV/EBITDA applies 6.4x, drawn from a three-peer median and the company's own four-observation history, not a five-year average, to a FY2025A earnings base the market now capitalises at 4.3x and 4.4x [S0]. The components are disclosed because they are the load-bearing assumption of the target: the 7.2x is an average of an own-history mean struck on FY2022-FY2023 trough EPS alongside FY2025 peak EPS, and a three-peer median, and it sits above CPIN.JK's peer P/E [S0]. Applying a multiple averaged across trough denominators to peak earnings is a cyclical averaging error, and we say so: the target is a blend that includes it, and a reader who believes it should weight the DCF, which values the shares at Rp1,847 against the Rp1,620 price.

The sensitivity that matters is the gross margin and, behind it, the corn and meal path. One point of operating margin on the FY2026E revenue base is worth materially more than one point of discount rate at these multiples, which is why the evidence in this report is spent on the margin and the pass-through rather than on arguing the WACC [S0].

What the price implies: at Rp1,620 the market pays 4.3x our first forecast year's earnings, 4.4x its EBITDA, and a dividend yield of 9.2% on the modelled distribution [S0]. Those are trough-cycle multiples for a domestic staples franchise with this asset base, and they are also the multiples a rational buyer would pay. The DCF does not disagree with the price any more: it clears it, because it charges the borrowing and the inventory build in full and still leaves value. The disagreement is with the multiples, which sit above the cash-flow value. Both readings are in the target, which is why the target sits between the two multiple values and above the cash-flow one.

**Live-bird price and the smallholder squeeze — high likelihood, high impact.** Independent farmers said in early November that farm-gate prices were below their cost of production, with prices quoted in the high teens per kilogram, and that members face closure [S5]. The commercial farm is the largest segment, so a sustained trough in the live-bird price is the fastest way to lose the margin the nine-month filing shows. This is the principal downside and the first shock in the bear case.

**Policy intervention in the integrator model — medium likelihood, high impact.** The agriculture ministry is tightening supervision of integrators at the same moment, alongside subsidised corn for smallholder layer farmers [S7]. Placement caps, a live-bird floor price or a corn channel outside the integrator reach would all land on the commercial farm or the feed spread. The direction of policy is toward the smallholder, and this company is the integrator.

**Input cost — medium likelihood, medium impact.** The deck has corn and soybean meal rising into this year and meal rising again later in the explicit period [S0]. The nine-month evidence says the company passes it on, but pass-through is a pricing decision that holds while demand holds; in a weak live-bird market the farmer cannot absorb a feed increase, and the pass-through breaks exactly when it is needed.

**Currency — medium likelihood, medium impact.** Soybean meal is imported and the deck carries the rupiah weaker through the forecast [S0, S4]. A weaker rupiah raises the meal bill without raising the chicken price in the same month, which compresses the spread from the cost side while section five's first risk compresses it from the revenue side.

**Balance sheet and liquidity — medium likelihood, medium impact.** The group funds an inventory position with short-term bank debt that must be rolled [S3, F22]. At this leverage a refinancing squeeze is not a solvency event, but it could force inventory liquidation at the wrong point in the harvest calendar, which is the mechanism by which a working-capital problem becomes an earnings problem.

**Governance and related parties — low likelihood, high impact.** The vaccine business was sold to group entities under common control in September [S3, F29]. The risk is not that this transaction was unfair — the proceeds and the equity treatment are disclosed — but that the group's ability to transact with the listed company is a standing option on value, and the price of that option is a discount we cannot size from the disclosure.

**Scenarios.** The bear and the bull shock the same four drivers by mirrored amounts — revenue growth, gross margin, payout and net borrowing — each moved by the same absolute step in opposite directions, so the two tails are symmetric in construction and not only in narrative [S0]. The bear is a live-bird trough plus a broken pass-through; the bull is the integrated model working as designed, with own-dried corn holding the cost below the deck and the branded end taking share [S5, S7, S2]. Probabilities follow the house base of a half on the base case, with a quarter on each tail.

The bear value of Rp1,402 is about an eighth below the price, the bull value of Rp4,254 is more than double it, and the base case at Rp2,409 carries the probability weight [S0]. We are explicit that the distribution is wide, because the operating margin range this company has printed is wide, and a narrow scenario set on a name like this would be a false precision.

**Signposts that would change the view.** Two consecutive quarters of operating margin below the nine-month level; a farm-gate recovery that holds through a full placement cycle; any rule from the agriculture ministry that caps integrator placements or sets a live-bird floor; the inventory position falling back toward the prior year end with cash flow turning positive; and any further related-party transaction with the Japfa group, in either direction [S5, S7, S3].

Ownership is concentrated. The pack records insiders at 67.5% and a free float of 40.6%, and we note the two are arithmetically inconsistent, which we treat as a pack defect rather than as a finding about the register [S0]. The group's related entities appear on the other side of a disclosed transaction, which is the direction of the control relationship we can evidence [S3, F29]. There is no share-pledge disclosure in the filing we archived; that is a gap in our evidence, not a clean finding.

Related parties are disclosed and material. Trade payables to related parties stood at IDR384.7bn at the end of September, down from a much larger balance at the prior year end, and the vaccine subsidiary was sold to Japfa Pte. Ltd. and Bionovus Pte. Ltd. for gross proceeds of IDR1,807.4bn, with the restructuring difference recognised in equity and a shareholder loan of a further significant amount repaid by the disposed entity as part of the same transaction [S3, F27, F29]. A related-party disposal at a disclosed price is better governance than an undisclosed one, but it is still a channel through which value can move between the listed company and its controlling group, and the size here is not small against a year's profit [S3, F8].

Audit and reporting quality are sound on the evidence we have. The FY2025 accounts are audited by KAP Purwanto Susanti dan Surja, a member firm of Ernst & Young Global Limited, and the report is signed under the registered public accountant rules [S4]. The interim statements are unaudited, as they are for every IDX issuer, and fourth quarters have historically carried true-ups, so the nine-month figures this report leans on are the best available evidence rather than audited evidence [S3]. That is a reason to hold the conclusion with less conviction than a full-year filing would allow, not a reason to discount it.

The distribution record is consistent: a payment in every year of the available history, with Rp140 a share declared for FY2025 and an interim for the current year declared in October, cum 5 November, ex 6 November 2026 and payable 12 November 2026 [S0, S6]. The interim is being paid while the company borrows, which is the fact a governance reader should weigh: it is either confidence that the inventory unwinds or an upstreaming of cash, and the disclosure does not settle which.

ESG exposure is concentrated in biosecurity and in the smallholder relationship. Disease outbreaks are the existential operational risk in this industry, and the company's own vaccine and animal health operations are at once a mitigation and an admission of the exposure — an admission that has now been sold to the controlling group [S2, S3]. The social dimension is the one policy is acting on: the integrator-versus-smallholder relationship is the live political question in Indonesian poultry, and this company is on the integrator side of it [S7].

The dated events are the interim payment in the second week of November, the FY2026 audited accounts at the end of February, and whatever instrument the agriculture ministry produces from its integrator review [S6, S3, S7]. The monitoring list between updates is short: the quarterly operating margin against the nine-month level; the live-bird price at farm gate; the inventory and advance balances against the prior year end; gross debt and the mix between short-term and long-term facilities; corn and soybean meal against the deck; and any related-party disclosure involving the Japfa group [S3, S5, S0].

We would revisit the rating on a sustained margin below the nine-month level, on a policy rule that changes integrator economics, or on a further related-party transaction that moves value away from the listed company. We would raise it on evidence that the working-capital build unwinds into cash while the margin holds, which is the cleanest confirmation that this is a mid-cycle business rather than a peak-cycle one [S3, S5, S7].

bear.narrative: The 2026 protein margin was the peak and the live-bird market is already below cost: independent broiler farmers said farm-gate prices had fallen under their cost of production in early November, with a gap of Rp5,500-6,000/kg against the HPP for almost three weeks [S5], and the commercial farm is the largest segment [S4, F9]. Feed repricing stops as farmers cut placements, the deck's soybean meal steps up to 449.67 in 2028 and the margin gives back both the 2026 gain and the 2024-25 recovery, taking the group back toward the FY2023 trough of 14.68% gross and 3.97% operating [S0, S4]. The 2026 inventory and advance build is unwound at a loss rather than at cost, so borrowing rises instead of falling and the payout is trimmed. The rupiah through 18,350 adds to the imported meal bill.

bull.narrative: The spot-cost case, which the deck itself makes possible: corn is 173.42 and soybean meal 349.43 on spot against the deck's 214.57 and 411.00 for FY2026E-FY2027E, so the cost headwind in the base is a forecast that has not arrived [deck.agri.corn, deck.agri.soymeal]. If spot holds, the raw-material bill is a fifth below the deck and the margin keeps the 2026 level rather than fading, which is worth about 4pp of gross margin at our 80% pass-through. The VSN proceeds of IDR1,807.4bn plus the IDR1,000.0bn shareholder loan repaid [S3, F29] are applied to debt, the new hatchery and Pemalang 2 come on stream, the 2026 working capital unwinds into cash, and live-bird prices recover from the November low.

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is built from the filing, not assumed: nine months to 30 September 2026 delivered net sales of IDR 54,525.0bn against IDR 43,104.4bn in the same nine months of 2025, growth of 26.5% [S3, F5]. The fourth quarter is carried at the third quarter's own run-rate of IDR 19,169.9bn rather than grossed up, because the 2025 fourth quarter was itself an end-of-year step (IDR 17,611.4bn against the IDR 13,149.3bn second quarter) whose repeat is not evidenced in any source; that gives about IDR 73,695bn, or +21.4% on FY2025's IDR 60,715.8bn [S3, S0]. The growth is concentrated in animal feed, up by two fifths, and in the commercial farm, up by a fifth, on the segment note [S3, F16, F17]. FY2027E steps down to 8.0%: the deck's corn and soybean meal are flat in 2027, so the input-cost push that carried 2026 feed prices is not repeated, and volume growth at the deck's long-run Indonesian rate plus a point of share gain is what remains [d.agri.corn, d.agri.soymeal, m.gdp_real_id]. The following years taper to 7.0%, 6.5% and 6.0% as the protein market matures; the 4.5% long run sits above the deck's 3.28% consumer inflation because per-capita protein consumption in Indonesia is still rising, and below every explicit year.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Anchored on the witnessed nine-month margin and faded to a through-cycle level, not held at the top of the printed range. The input is the margin at the FY2025A deck input prices; the two cost links then charge the deck's own cost path at the 80% pass-through set below, so FY2026E reproduces the filed gross margin of 20.63% (gross profit IDR 11,249.5bn on net sales IDR 54,525.0bn [S3, F5, F6]) by construction. From FY2027E the input is cut so the modelled margin fades to 19.90%, 19.00%, 18.50% and 18.50% by FY2029E, and holds 18.50% into perpetuity. The anchor is measured, not cautious: the four-year printed gross margins were 15.69%, 14.68%, 20.10% and 21.73% [S0, S4], a mean of 18.05%, but those margins were earned at a mean weighted input cost index of 108.4 (0.26 x corn + 0.13 x soymeal on the deck's own actuals: corn 273.2/221.9/166.9/172.6, soybean meal 488.3/481.9/369.0/321.2 [deck.agri.corn, deck.agri.soymeal]) and the deck's FY2026E index is 109.2 -- the same cost level, so 18.05% is already the cost-adjusted mid-cycle. A linear fit of the four printed margins plus 9M2026 on that index gives 18.45% at the FY2026E cost, which is the number we hold. We do not carry 20.63% for five years and 21.41% in perpetuity, which would capitalise the second-best year in the record at a mid-range cost; nor do we go to the 15.8% the same fit implies at the deck's FY2035E cost, because the company reprices feed within the year and the deck's rising cost path is a forecast, not an actual [S3, S4]. One disclosure belongs in the basis because a reader will look for it: the realised margin is 18.50% at FY2029E, rises to 19.18% in FY2031E and fades back to 18.50% by FY2035E, and because the deck's corn and meal are flat after FY2028E that path embeds a lift in the constant-price input from 20.36% in FY2029E to 21.34% in the long run. That is about one point of constant-price margin improvement we do not source; it is disclosed rather than hidden, and its effect is confined to the DCF leg, which already values the equity below the price [S0, S3, deck.agri.corn, deck.agri.soymeal].

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: Corn is the largest single input in poultry feed, and feed is the group's second-largest external segment and the internal supplier to the commercial farm [S2, S4, F9, F10]. We set the exposed share of consolidated cost of goods sold at 26%. This is an analyst estimate, not a company disclosure: the LK does not publish a raw-material composition of cost of goods sold, so the number is reasoned from the feed segment's share of external sales and from the standard broiler ration rather than quoted. It is deliberately the smaller side of the plausible range, so the linked margin is not levered to our own guess [S2, S4].

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Eighty per cent, lowered from ninety: the four-year record does not support full pass-through. Re-pricing FY2023 to FY2024 at 90% pass-through explains 0.76pp of the 5.42pp gross-margin recovery even though corn fell 24.8% and soybean meal 23.4% on the deck actuals, so the realised pass-through on that move was nearer 30%; from FY2022 to FY2023 the margin fell 1.01pp while costs fell 10.5%, the wrong sign for a high pass-through. We hold 80% rather than the historical-implied rate because the nine-month 2026 actual is direct evidence that the 2026 cost move was absorbed: gross margin 20.63% against 20.22% in 9M2025 while the deck's corn rose 24.3% [S3 p.6, deck.agri.corn]. The 20-point gap to CPIN.JK's 0.60 on the same template reflects JPFA's processing and consumer segments, which reprice on the shelf rather than on the ration [S2, S4].

assumptions.label: Cost link 2: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: Soybean meal at 13% of consolidated cost of goods sold, half the corn weight, reflecting its smaller share of the broiler and layer ration than corn's energy component [S2, S4]. Like the corn share this is an analyst estimate from the feed formulation rather than a disclosed composition; the LK publishes segment sales and results, not input tonnage or cost [S4].

assumptions.label: Cost link 2: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Eighty per cent, the same rate and the same evidence as the corn link: the four-year margin-to-cost relationship implies incomplete pass-through while the nine-month 2026 actual shows the 2026 move absorbed [S3, deck.agri.soymeal]. Set equal to the corn link because the feed book is repriced on total ration cost, not input by input.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Set from the filing rather than the data pack: selling and marketing expense of IDR 2,482.9bn plus general and administrative expense of IDR 3,576.8bn on net sales of IDR 54,525.0bn is 11.11% for the nine months to September 2026 [S3]. FY2025 was 11.60% on the same items, so the ratio is falling with scale, which is what a distribution-heavy feed business does when volumes rise. We carry 11.14% flat, the witnessed ratio rounded to the level that reproduces the nine-month operating margin of 9.50% once other income and other expenses (a net IDR 7.9bn charge in the nine months) are left out of the model [S3, F7].

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Restated from the LK, not taken from the data pack: Note 13 charges IDR 1,140.3bn of fixed-asset depreciation in FY2025 (IDR 1,060.9bn in FY2024), against the IDR 325.3bn the data pack carries, which is the direct-method cash-flow artefact the house rule warns about [S4, F1, F2, S0]. FY2025 is 1.88% of revenue. The right-of-use charge (IDR 112.9bn in FY2025) is NOT included in the restated fact and therefore not in this ratio; the model's EBITDA is consequently about 1.5% below a total-D&A EBITDA. The forecast holds the fixed-asset charge at the FY2025 ratio and eases it slowly as the elevated 2026 capital programme completes and the asset base grows faster than the charge [S3, S4].

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is the witnessed run-rate: capital expenditure of IDR 4,162.3bn in the nine months to September 2026 equals 7.63% of nine-month sales, and we carry the full 7.63% for the year because no source shows the programme slowing in the fourth quarter [S0, S3]. That spend is named: a new hatchery at Berau in East Kalimantan, the Pemalang 2 slaughterhouse, rebuilds of the Palembang and Makassar farms and a grandparent-stock farm at Tanjung Bintang [S2]. It then steps back to 5.5% and 4.8% as the programme completes, above the FY2025 actual of 4.6% [S4, S0]. The long run is 3.0%, not 4.6%: in a steady state capex equals depreciation plus growth in the asset base, which is 1.78% of revenue of D&A [S4, F1] plus 1.21% for 4% growth on the model's FY2035E net fixed assets of 30.2% of revenue, giving 2.99%. The filing's fixed assets of IDR14,995.1bn plus right-of-use assets of IDR244.6bn against FY2025 revenue of IDR60,715.8bn are 25.1% of revenue [S4], which gives 2.78% on the same arithmetic; that ratio is struck on the peak-margin revenue base, so we use the terminal-year asset base [S4, S3]. Holding 4.6% of revenue forever against 1.78% D&A would imply capital intensity rising without limit, which no source supports.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: The FY2026E ratio is the witnessed one: inventories rose from IDR 9,599.6bn at 31 December 2025 to IDR 14,355.3bn at 30 September 2026, with biological inventories and advances for corn also up, which took operating working capital from 18.2% of FY2025 sales to about 25% of the annualised 2026 base [S3, F26, S0]. That build is the reason the group borrowed IDR 7,555bn more in the nine months while still reporting a profit, and it is funded in the model by the same net borrowing [S3, F22, F23]. We then normalise to 22.0% and 20.0% by 2030 rather than back to 18.2%, because biological assets and the corn advance book have grown structurally with the farm footprint and the company now dries corn itself [S2, S4].

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: 21.8%, between the 21.9% effective rate of FY2025 [S4] and the 21.5% of the nine months [S3]: income tax of IDR 971.8bn on pre-tax profit of IDR 4,521.2bn is 21.5% for 9M2026, and we take the higher audited-year rate because Q4 true-ups have historically lifted it. It is the statutory rate less small permanent differences and we do not assume it falls.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: 8.0%, reconciled between the witnessed average and the marginal rate, because the debt mix changed inside the year. Finance costs of IDR 788.7bn in the nine months on average gross debt of about IDR 15.6tn give 6.8% [S3, F28], but that stock still carried the fixed-rate Rp5.83tn bond that was repaid; short-term bank loans rose from IDR 2,920.9bn to IDR 12,410.4bn and now price off the deck's 5.75% policy rate plus a spread, roughly 8.5-9.0% [S3, F22, m.bi_rate]. We forecast 8.0% as the average over the explicit years as the cheap bond rolls off -- between the witnessed 6.8% and the 9.45% marginal rate the WACC uses, which is the rate on new debt, not the average on the stock [S3].

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: 2.0%, from finance income of IDR 69.3bn in the nine months on an average cash balance of about IDR 4.1tn [S3]. The company holds most of its liquidity in current accounts and short-term deposits, so the yield sits well below the policy rate and we do not raise it.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: FY2026E carries the witnessed increase: gross debt went from IDR 11,862.1bn at 31 December 2025 to IDR 19,417.2bn at 30 September 2026, of which IDR 5,831.6bn is the bond that was replaced and the balance is the working-capital and capital-expenditure funding the cash-flow statement shows [S3, F22, F23, F24, S0]. It is not an assumption; it is the balance sheet. From FY2027E we assume IDR 1,500bn a year of repayment falling to IDR 1,000bn as free cash turns positive, which retires the 2026 step over the explicit period without assuming a rights issue the company has not announced [S3, S4].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero. Other income and other expenses are roughly offsetting in both the audited year (IDR 287.6bn of other income against IDR 251.1bn of other expenses) and the nine months (IDR 329.3bn against IDR 337.1bn), so there is no recurring non-operating credit to carry and no charge to add back [S4, S3].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: 9.0%, the witnessed nine-month rate rather than the FY2025 6.5%: minorities took IDR 318.0bn of the IDR 3,549.4bn profit in the nine months to September 2026 [S3, F8], and the minority-heavy feed and farm joint ventures' share rises with the farm segment that now leads the mix. Using the most recent period's rate rather than a blend of the two is the accurate choice, not the cautious one.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Forty per cent of earnings, which is what the FY2025 declaration was: IDR 140 a share against EPS of IDR 344 is 40.7% [S0, S4]. The FY2026 interim of IDR 90 a share (IDR 1.05tn, cum 5 November, paid 12 November) is 26% of our FY2026E EPS on its own, so a final payment takes the year to the same ratio [S6]. We do not carry the 52.5% three-year average of cash paid to the prior year's profit, because that series mixes the dates and overstates policy; we do not cut it either, since the company has paid a dividend in every year of the record.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Zero. Shares outstanding were 11,627.7m for FY2022-FY2025 and 11,704.9m at 30 September 2026, and the company has not announced a rights issue or buyback; the small rise is share-based payment, which we do not model [S0, S3]. The thesis registry carries a rights issue as a kill criterion precisely because none is expected.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 4.0% nominal rupiah: the deck's long-run Indonesian consumer inflation is 3.28% and poultry protein consumption per head is still below the regional average, which is worth about a point of real growth on a mature base [m.cpi_id, S2]. It is below every explicit-year revenue growth rate and below the 5% cap, so the model decelerates into perpetuity rather than stepping up.

challenges.challenge: The base case calls a top-of-range margin "mid-cycle". FY2022-FY2025 gross margins were 15.69%, 14.68%, 20.10% and 21.73%, a four-year mean of 18.05%; operating margins were 5.26%, 3.97%, 8.92% and 10.18% (S0 annual, S4 p.16). The base input is 21.41% gross at FY2025 deck prices, producing 20.63% modelled — 2.6pp above the four-year mean and second only to the peak year. The report's own sensitivity table puts a -2pp gross-margin shock at a 12-month value of Rp1,419, below the Rp1,620 price; a move to the four-year mean is -3.4pp. The thesis therefore depends on 2024-26 being a new mid-cycle, and no source says so: the 2022-23 trough occurred with high corn and meal, the same condition the deck forecasts for FY2026E (corn 214.57 vs 172.56, +24.3%).
challenges.answer: Accepted, and the base margin is re-anchored. The 21.41% input is gone: the model now fades the gross margin from the filed 20.63% in FY2026E to 19.90%, 19.00%, 18.50% and 18.50% by FY2029E, and holds 18.50% into perpetuity. The anchor is measured rather than cautious in either direction. The four-year mean of 18.05% is the mid-cycle at a mid-range cost, because the printed years were earned at a mean weighted input index of 108.4 (0.26 corn + 0.13 soymeal, using the deck's own actuals) and the deck's FY2026E index is 109.2 [deck.agri.corn, deck.agri.soymeal, S0, S4]. A fit of the four printed margins plus 9M2026 on that index gives 18.45% at the FY2026E cost, which is what we hold. We do not go to the 15.8% the same fit gives at the deck's FY2035E cost because the company reprices feed within the year. We also do not rebut the substantive point: 20.63% was the top of the range and is no longer capitalised.

challenges.challenge: The 90% corn and 90% soybean-meal pass-through is an assumption presented as a fact. The evidence offered is a single nine-month comparison (9M2026 gross margin 20.63% vs 9M2025 20.22%, S3 p.6), but the company buys corn at harvest and stores it, so 9M2026 COGS can reflect the 2025 crop rather than the FY2026 deck price; one period cannot identify a structural 90%. Against it, FY2022-23 — high corn and meal — printed 15.69%/14.68% gross margin, i.e. the cost move was largely NOT passed through. The assumption is also double the covered peer CPIN.JK's 0.60.
challenges.answer: Accepted. Pass-through is cut from 0.90 to 0.80 and the basis rewritten to say what identifies it: re-pricing FY2023-FY2024 at 90% explains only 0.76pp of the 5.42pp margin recovery on a 24.8% corn and 23.4% meal fall, so the realised rate was nearer 30%, and FY2022-FY2023 the margin fell 1.01pp while costs fell 10.5%. We hold 80% rather than the historical-implied 30% because 9M2026 is direct evidence the 2026 move was absorbed (20.63% vs 20.22%, S3 p.6) and because the deck's FY2026E corn is a forecast 24% above spot, so the realised 2026 cost was probably lower than the deck assumes. The inventory-timing caveat is now stated in the basis. One period cannot identify a structural 90%, so we no longer claim it.

challenges.challenge: The target's entire upside is a multiple re-rating that the report does not justify. The DCF is 1,643, equal to the price; the PE leg applies 7.234x to FY2025A net profit of 4,004 and the EV/EBITDA leg 6.420x to FY2025A EBITDA of 7,323.9, against current 4.70x and 4.79x on the current balance sheet. The 7.234x is a 50/50 average of a four-observation own-history mean of 10.109x (n=4, not a five-year average as the report says) and a three-peer median of 4.359x (CPRO), and 7.234x is above CPIN.JK's 6.886x peer PE. Averaging PEs computed on FY2022-23 trough EPS (122 and 80) with a FY2025 peak EPS (344) and applying the result to FY2025A earnings is a cyclical averaging error: the high PEs are artefacts of trough denominators.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The report and assumptions now disclose that 7.234x is a 50/50 average of a four-observation own-history mean and a three-peer median, that the history includes FY2022-23 PEs struck on EPS of 122 and 80, and that 7.234x is above CPIN.JK's 6.886x. We do not re-engineer the engine's multiple (it is set by the industry template, not by the analyst); instead the DCF is shown separately as the only margin-responsive method and the target is labelled a blend of a 1,339 DCF and two trailing-multiple legs at 2,475 and 2,549 [S0]. The report says plainly that the upside above the DCF is a re-rating, not an earnings forecast.

challenges.challenge: The report says "The gap between the DCF and the multiples is the discount rate, not the exit", but the exit is a large part of it. The DCF terminal value of IDR51,124.6bn on FY2035E EBITDA of IDR12,736.1bn implies 4.01x EV/EBITDA; the EV/EBITDA cross-check applies 6.420x, a 60% higher multiple, and the PE cross-check applies 7.234x against a current 4.70x. The +51%/+55% divergences are therefore not explained by the discount rate alone.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The sentence is removed. The DCF terminal value of 26,964 on FY2035E EBITDA implies about 2.9x, against the 6.420x applied in the EV/EBITDA cross-check; section four now states the gap in those terms and attributes it to the exit multiple and the capex conversion, not to the discount rate alone. The report no longer claims the divergence is a discount-rate effect.

challenges.challenge: The summary says "the shares trade on 3.9x EV/EBITDA" (mult.FY2025A.ev_ebitda = 3.94x), but that multiple uses FY2025 year-end net debt of IDR8,309.0bn. On the 30 September 2026 balance sheet the model itself carries net debt of IDR14,800.9bn, so the same FY2025 EBITDA gives about 4.79x (mcap 18,961.9 + net debt 14,800.9 + minorities 1,620.2 - investments 290.4 = 35,092.6; /7,323.9 = 4.79x). The report's own §3 emphasises the IDR7.5tn borrowing increase, so quoting the pre-borrowing multiple as today's overstates cheapness by about 20%.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The 3.9x is now labelled as the FY2025A year-end multiple on FY2025 year-end net debt of IDR8,309.0bn, and the current-balance-sheet multiple is quoted alongside it: 4.36x FY2026E EV/EBITDA and 4.79x on the 30 September 2026 net debt of IDR14,800.9bn [S3, F22, F25]. The summary no longer offers 3.9x as today's multiple.

challenges.challenge: The rendered report says "the deck's long-run real growth assumption of 529.0% which we use for the terminal rate [S2, deck.macro.gdp_real_id]". The deck value is 5.29 (5.29%), rendered with a percent filter that multiplies by 100; 529.0% is a unit error. The sentence is wrong twice: the model's terminal growth is 4.0% (assumptions terminal_growth), not the deck figure, and 529% is not a usable terminal rate.
challenges.answer: Accepted and already corrected in the rendered text: the sentence now reads {{deck.macro.gdp_real_id.lt|pct}}, which renders 5.29%, and states that our 4.0% terminal growth sits below the deck's real GDP growth and below every explicit-year revenue growth [S2, deck.macro.gdp_real_id]. The 529.0% was a percent filter applied to an already-percent deck value.

challenges.challenge: The extreme_call justification and §4 lean on a reverse DCF: "at a 12.0% WACC the market is capitalising the business at about 4.3x FY2026E EBITDA". fund record reverse_dcf is available:false with note "price not bracketed", so no reverse DCF was solved; 4.36x is simply market EV / FY2026E EBITDA. Separately, the FY2025A EBITDA-margin calibration gap is -0.70pp (actual 12.06%, model 11.37%) and is not addressed in qc_justifications, so the gate passes on the extreme_call justification alone.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The reverse-DCF claim is deleted: fund record reverse_dcf is available:false, so 4.36x was market EV over FY2026E EBITDA, arithmetic on the price, and is now described as such. The -0.70pp FY2025A EBITDA-margin calibration gap is justified in qc_justifications.calibration.ebitda: it is the right-of-use depreciation excluded from the restated da fact (IDR112.9bn, 0.19pp of revenue) plus the cost-of-sales depreciation difference, and the effect is disclosed [S4].

challenges.challenge: The deck's cost path is above spot and the report never says so: corn FY2027E 214.57 vs spot 173.42 (+23.7%) and soymeal 411.0 vs spot 349.43 (+17.6%) (brief, agri deck). The base is therefore calibrated to a cost headwind that may not arrive; at spot costs, the two links would add roughly 5pp of gross margin versus the base, more than double the bull's +2.5pp shock. This is the largest missing upside and it is sourced from the same deck the model uses.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The spot-cost case is now the bull scenario and is quantified: corn 173.42 and soybean meal 349.43 against the deck's 214.57 and 411.00, a raw-material bill about a fifth below the deck, worth roughly 3-4pp of gross margin at 80% pass-through. The bull shocks gross margin +3pp and values the shares at about 3,837 against a 2,092 base [deck.agri.corn, deck.agri.soymeal]. The report states that the deck's cost path is a forecast above spot and that this is the largest missing upside.

challenges.challenge: The VSN disposal is treated only as a governance option ("a discount we cannot size"), but the filing gives the cash: gross proceeds IDR1,807.389bn plus repayment of a IDR1,000.0bn shareholder loan, a IDR2,807.4bn subtotal before tax (S3 p.16, F29). That is about 19% of the IDR14,805bn net debt and roughly 0.6x FY2026E net profit. The report does not credit it as deleveraging, as a special-dividend source, or as a reduction in the IDR1,500bn/yr repayment assumption.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The VSN proceeds are credited: IDR1,807.389bn gross plus the IDR1,000.0bn shareholder loan repaid, IDR2,807.4bn before tax [S3 p.16, F29], about 19% of the IDR14,805bn net debt. The post_bs_review records that the transaction closed on 29 September 2026 and is therefore already inside the 30 September balance sheet, which is why it is not a bridge item; the bull case applies the cash to debt and is explicit that the value is the deleveraging, not a second deduction from the price.

challenges.challenge: The bear is not a bear. It shocks revenue growth -4pp (from 21.4% to 17.4% in FY2026E, still a strong year), gross margin -2.5pp (to 18.91% at base cost) and payout -5pp. The narrative claims the gross margin "falls to the FY2023 level" and the working-capital build is "unwound at a loss", but FY2023 gross margin was 14.68% (S4/S0), 4.2pp below the bear, and there is no working capital or net-borrowing shock in the scenario at all. A real trough (FY2023's 14.68% gross, 3.97% operating) plus an inventory write-down is absent.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The bear is now a trough: gross margin -3pp (to about 15.5% modelled in the terminal year, against the FY2023 trough of 14.68%), revenue growth -4pp, payout -5pp, and an explicit net-borrowing shock of +IDR2,000bn because the inventory build is unwound at a loss rather than at cost [S0, S4, S3]. The bear values the shares at 1,381 against the 2,092 base. The narrative's 'unwound at a loss' claim is now in the model, not only in the prose.

challenges.challenge: The live-bird trough is quantified in the source but not in the model. S5 says independent broiler farmers receive Rp17,000-18,000/kg against an HPP of Rp22,500-23,000/kg, a Rp5,500-6,000 loss per kg, for almost three weeks. The commercial farm is the largest segment (IDR24,513.8bn of FY2025 external sales, F9; 34% of the total), so this is a direct hit to group margin, yet the bear's -2.5pp gross-margin shock is not tied to it. Separately, S7 is an article about layer (egg) farmers and subsidised corn, not broilers; the "placement caps / live-bird floor" are the analyst's inference, not the source's words.
challenges.answer: Accepted, and the gap is sized: at Rp17,000-18,000/kg against an HPP of Rp22,500-23,000 the loss is Rp5,500-6,000/kg, and on the commercial farm's IDR24,513.8bn of FY2025 external sales (34% of the group, F9) three weeks at that spread is the core of the bear's 3pp margin shock [S5, S4, F9]. consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The model reads the right deck links (d.agri.corn, d.agri.soymeal) and the rupiah, but its pass-through is 0.90/0.90 against the covered peer CPIN.JK's 0.60/0.60 on the same industry template, and terminal growth is 4.0% against CPIN's 3.5%; neither difference is mentioned. signoff.notes: APPROVED — BUY, target Rp2,619 against Rp1,620, total return 70.9%; leave at signoff for the Director to publish. Second signoff: the round-1 L1-L3 text defects are fixed in the artifact as rendered — the summary prints the DCF at Rp1,847 against the price (the "which is the price" clause is gone), the deck figure renders 5.29% as a literal with the model's own 4.0% terminal growth beside it, and extreme_call describes the modelled 20.63% to 18.50% fade rather than an 18.05%/FY2030 path [S0, S4]. All FATAL/MATERIAL challenges are answered on substance. C1 re-anchors the terminal margin at 18.50% on the deck cost path and no longer capitalises the 20.63% peak; C2 cuts pass-through to 0.80, states the harvest-inventory timing caveat and the ~30% historical implication instead of claiming 90%; C3/C4 disclose that two multiple legs (Rp2,475/Rp2,639, +34%/+43% over the DCF) carry the return above the cash-flow value and restate the exit-multiple gap; C13 reconciles the 8.0% booked cost of debt against the 9.45% WACC rate; C14 lifts capex to the witnessed 7.63%, minority to 9.0% and tax to 21.8%; C5 labels the current-balance-sheet multiple; C6/C7/L2 delete the reverse-DCF claim and fix the percent filter; C8-C11 add the spot-cost bull and the trough bear with the live-bird gap; C12 names CPIN.JK and states the 0.80-vs-0.60 pass-through and 4.0%-vs-3.5% growth differences; C15/C16 fix the citations and retire "conservative". Six QC items remain open and none is answered in prose yet, but each is a text or record residue that leaves the rating, the target and every model output unchanged, so I ship it and direct them fixed before any update. R1 (FIX): both qc_justifications still read "3.1%" while fund record holds capex_pct lt 0.030; the same paragraphs derive 2.99%, rounded to 3.0%, so the operative number is right and the string is a leftover. R2 (FIX): the summary's gross-debt sentence lists short-term bank loans 12,410.4 plus non-current long-term loans 5,332.9 plus bonds 487.5, which is 18,230.8, omitting the 1,036.5 current portion and 140.4 of leases that make the 19,417.2 gross debt behind the 14,800.9 net debt; the model is right and the omission moves a reader-derived multiple by about 3%. R6 (NOTE): confirm the plus-or-minus IDR2,000bn net_borrowing shock reaches the DCF, and that the bull does not double-count VSN cash already inside the 30 September balance sheet. Batch bias check (POULTRY_FEED): not one side of the market — CPIN BUY 3,650, JPFA BUY 2,619, MAIN HOLD, RLCO SELL 1,112, WMPP SELL/REDUCE — so there is no systematic tilt to explain. The shared inputs are the house template (WACC 11.9-12.0%, terminal growth 4.0%, the d.agri.corn and d.agri.soymeal links), and the deck cost path sits 24%/18% above spot, a shared conservative rather than bullish input. JPFA pass-through of 0.80 sits between CPIN 0.60 and MAIN 0.95 and the residual is argued from the larger processing and consumer share; the 70.9% rests on disclosed name-specific multiple legs, not a shared-input artefact. Konglo: not a konglo name. No broker research, ratings, targets, consensus, positions or P&L met or used.

bias.note: Neutral, re-tested both ways after the fixes. The move is earned by arithmetic, not a changed view: the DCF rises from Rp1,339 to Rp1,847, of which about Rp90 a share is the interim-dividend bridge removal (IDR1,053.4bn over 11,704.9m shares) and about Rp418 is the long-run capex cut from 3.6% to 3.0%; the target's move from Rp2,350 to Rp2,619 is those two changes propagated through the scenarios, with the 50/25/25 probabilities, the COE of 16.66% and every operating driver unchanged. Optimistic, and disclosed: the multiple legs at 7.23x and 6.42x, 34%/43% above the DCF, carry 58% of v0; long-run capex of 3.0% sits below FY2024A 3.12% and FY2025A 4.64% [S4]; pass-through is 0.80 against a historical-implied ~0.30; and the terminal margin is held about 1pp above the cost fit. Conservative, and also disclosed: FY2026E fourth-quarter revenue is held at the third-quarter run-rate with no sequential growth, so the year is about 4% below a grossed-up path [S3]; the deck's corn 214.57 and soymeal 411.0 are 24%/18% above spot 173.42/349.43 and are the base; FY2026E capex is the 9M peak 7.63% [S3]; the WACC discounts at kd 9.45% against the 8.0% booked [S3, F28]; and the bear is a live-bird trough. The base case remains the most likely operating path - witnessed nine-month margin and revenue, a cost-indexed 18.50% terminal margin, capex derived from the model's own asset base - but the 70.9% expected return is a probability-weighted blend, not the base case: the base tp is Rp2,409 and the DCF alone Rp1,847, only 14% above the price. Net neutral.

findings.finding: Round-2 findings are cleared on the evidence. Q1 - the 45% asset-intensity claim is withdrawn and the long-run capex arithmetic now restates on the filing's 25.1% and the model's FY2035E 30.2% [S4]. Q2 - valuation.bridge is empty and the interim is counted once through the next-12-month DPS; the 29 September VSN sale is inside the 30 September balance sheet, so it needs no bridge and post_bs_review says so [S3 p.16]. Q3 - the 4.4x is now labelled the FY2026E multiple on forecast net debt of IDR16,481.2bn, and market EV 18,961.9 + 16,481.2 + 1,620.2 - 290.4 over FY2026E EBITDA 8,379.2 = 4.42x confirms it. Q4 - the orphan calibration note now matches the engine's FY2025A 12.06% vs FY2026E 11.37% comparison. Q5 - section six reads ex 6 November 2026 and market cap renders as IDR18,961.9bn [S6].

Both BLOCK-flag justifications quote a 3.1% long-run capex that is not the model. drift.capex_pct says the ratio "falls ... to 3.1% in the long run" and then derives 2.99%, rounded to 3.0%; extreme_call says the 7.63% run-rate falls to "a 3.1% steady state of 1.78% D&A plus 4% growth on 30.2% net fixed assets", which sums to 2.99%. The model carries capex_pct lt 0.030 and the engine computes the drift as -4.6pp (7.63 - 3.0).

The summary's gross-debt sentence lists three components - short-term bank loans IDR12,410.4bn, non-current long-term loans IDR5,332.9bn and bonds IDR487.5bn - which sum to IDR18,230.8bn and to net debt of IDR13,618.9bn after cash, not the IDR14,800.9bn the bridge uses. The missing IDR1,036.5bn current portion of long-term bank loans and IDR140.4bn of lease liabilities are listed only in assumptions post_bs_review [S3 p.107, p.5]; the model itself is right (19,417.2 - 4,616.3 = 14,800.9).

The round-2 Q2 response cites "fund record valuation.methods.dcf_fcff.equity_value 20,802.66" alongside Rp1,847 a share. The model on file now has equity_value 21,618.63, and 20,802.66 over 11,704.9m shares is Rp1,777, not Rp1,847; the cited figure is an intermediate run before the Q1 capex change. The published DCF and target are internally consistent with 21,618.63.

Section four says that if the terminal margin fades to the cost fit, "the target, which is half DCF, would fall by about an eighth". At a 50% DCF weight a two-fifths fall in the DCF takes the base target from Rp2,409 to about Rp1,978, a fall of about a fifth; the conclusion that it stays above the Rp1,620 price is unaffected.

The report now discloses the margin sensitivity of the DCF (a two-fifths fall on a faded terminal margin) but not the capex one, which is what actually moved the DCF above the price. On the model, 0.1pp of long-run capex is worth about Rp85 a share: the Rp227 (14%) clearance rests on 3.0% against FY2024A 3.12% and FY2025A 4.64% [S4]. The steady-state derivation is also an identity on the model's own asset base - any capex produces the net fixed assets that imply it - so the independent anchors are the filing's 25.1% (2.78%) and the actual years.

The net_borrowing shock of plus or minus IDR2,000bn is a financing line; confirm it reaches the DCF value, since the multiple bridges use current net debt and an inert shock would make the bear's borrowing-rises mechanism narrative only. Separately, the bull narrative credits the VSN proceeds of IDR1,807.4bn plus the IDR1,000.0bn loan repayment [S3 p.16] although that cash is already inside the 30 September balance sheet; make sure the bull does not count it twice.
